problem:
For the function

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s(s+3)},\,s>-3
$$

find the inverse Laplace transform of $G(s),$ given that
$L{{e}^{at}}=\frac{1}{s-a},\text{ }s>a.$

feedback.problem:
For the function

$$
G(s)=\frac{6}{{s}^{5}},\,s>0
$$

find the inverse Laplace transform of $G(s),$ given that
$L{{t}^{n}}=\frac{n!}{{s}^{n+1}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that we can write $G(s)$ as 

$$
G(s)=\frac{6}{{s}^{5}}=\frac{F(s)}{s},
$$

where $F(s)=\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}.$
Also, we know that

$$
L{{t}^{n}}=\frac{n!}{{s}^{n+1}}.
$$

Thus, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{F(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{3!}{{s}^{3+1}}} \\  & ={t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Additionally, we know that if $L{f(t)}=F(s)$, then

$$
L{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{G(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{F(s)}{s}} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}{τ}^{3}\,\text{d}τ \\  & =\frac{{t}^{4}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
